I've fixed the bug: `echo '![x\"x](x)' | python -m markdown -x smarty` now outputs `

`, the same as the unescaped version. Nothing is committed. **Root cause:** A backslash escape like `\"` is stored as a placeholder while the document is processed. That placeholder was only turned back into `"` after the HTML had been written out, so the step that escapes attribute values never saw the quote and wrote a raw `"` into `alt`. Smarty makes `"` and `'` escapable, which is why it exposed the bug. An escaped `>` already had the same problem without smarty. **Fix:** I added an `UnescapeTreeprocessor` in `markdown/treeprocessors.py` that restores escaped characters before the HTML is written. The normal escaping then handles them. It covers text, tails and every attribute, and skips the text of `` elements. I kept the old after-output unescape step, because inline raw HTML can still contain placeholders. A delegated first attempt patched only the attributes built by link and image patterns. It missed `# h {: title="a\"b" }` with attr_list, which still produced `title="a"b"`, so I discarded it and wrote this more general fix. **Fixed cases** (all produced invalid HTML before): - **Image alt text**, inline and reference-style: `\"`, and `\>` even without smarty. - **Link and image titles:** `\"`. - **attr_list attribute values:** `\"`. - **Text content:** `\"` was already valid there and still renders as `"`. **One visible output change:** an escaped `>` in body text now renders as `>` instead of `>`. It means the same thing and is valid HTML, but anyone comparing output byte-for-byte will see a difference. I updated `tests/basic/backlash-escapes.html` to match. **Tests and docs:** - New `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_smarty.py` covering alt text, titles, reference images, plain text and attr_list. - Escaped `>` cases in `tests/test_syntax/inline/test_images.py`. - A unit test for the new processor in `tests/test_apis.py`. - A note in `docs/change_log/release-3.4.md` and a row in the processor table in `docs/extensions/api.md`. **Test results:** pytest gives `4 failed, 679 passed, 129 skipped`. The 4 failures are in `test_html_blocks.py` and fail the same way without my changes. pytest can't load `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_md_in_html.py` at all (also true before my change), so I ran with `--ignore` for that file. The project's unittest runner, which does load it, shows the same 4 old failures again from that file. flake8 isn't installed in the venv, so I didn't run a lint check.
